title: Common cylinder divisor tests give identical success thresholds
statement: Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and let $E$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] transverse to $N$ (its local equations restrict to distinct coordinate parameters on $N$). Let $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ be coherent and $d\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q\ge0:I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with value $\infty$ for zero, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(I,d)=\{x:\operatorname{ord}_xI\ge d\}$. A test transformation is an open restriction, a smooth-center blowup in cosupport with normal crossings with $E$, a product with a line adjoining its zero section to $E$, or a blowup of the intersection of two boundary hypersurfaces. For a cosupport blowup use the strict transform of $N$ and the ideal $e^{-d}\sigma^*I$, where $e$ is the exceptional equation; for the last two operations use ordinary pullback. Two such data on the same ambient scheme and with the same ordered boundary are test equivalent if their finite test sequences coincide. Let $(N,I,d)$ and $(P,J,b)$ be test equivalent, where $P$ is also smooth and has the same local dimension as $N$.  After any common finite sequence [def-trf-common-marked-test-sequence], write $(T,M_T,P_T)$ for its endpoints, $d_T,b_T$ for their marks, and take arbitrary support points $x\in M_T$, $y\in P_T$ with the same ambient image in both cosupports. Put $m=\operatorname{ord}_x I_T$ and $n=\operatorname{ord}_y J_T$. For every $k\ge1$ and $i\ge0$, the two inequalities $((k+i+1)d_T:\mathbb N_\infty)\le k m$ and $((k+i+1)b_T:\mathbb N_\infty)\le k n$ are equivalent. All products are in the extended natural numbers, so this also specifies the zero-ideal case.

proof.text: Induct on a common prefix: the depth-wise definition of restricted equivalence passes every finite suffix to its endpoints and gives equality of their cosupports already at depth zero. No upper-semicontinuity or closed-point-density argument is needed to recover this equality. Coordinate charts preserve smoothness, finite type and the boundary conditions. The finite-type dimension formula and equality of support residue fields with the ambient residue field preserve equal local support dimensions, as in original step 11.

proof.text: At the common point take the simultaneous smooth generic-center normal slice. Separate completions use the same residue field and the same number of normal variables, and preserve the two ideal orders. Shrinking permits the smooth centers required by each fixed finite word. Boundary components may be split into their locally relevant smooth components before using the integral-label version of the slice statement.

proof.text: Adjoin a line and perform k section blowups. In the t chart the controlled ideal is t^(-kd)K(t^k u). The isotropic calculation gives order (k+1)m-kd at the next section, at least d on cosupport, so each finite section tower is permissible. The zero ideal and zero-dimensional normal slice are covered by the zero clauses of that calculation.

proof.text: The next divisor test asks if the newest exceptional divisor meets cosupport in its full local dimension. Its local ring is a regular local domain; a proper closed germ has smaller dimension by quotienting a nonzerodivisor. Thus both supports give the same answer using their common cosupport and equal local dimension. Success is precisely containment in the dth divisor power. The controlled chart theorem then permits the common divisor-center blowup, which divides by that power.

proof.text: Repeat the divisor-center blowup only while its test succeeds. After i successful divisions the next success is k(m-d)>=(i+1)d, or equivalently (k+i+1)d<=km; the isotropic formula gives this precise criterion and gives success always for the zero ideal. Equality of the geometric answers yields the displayed iff. Earlier failed tests cannot hide a later success since the inequalities decrease with i.

lean.statement: theorem cylinder_test_thresholds (S : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (M P : Marked S) [LocallyOfFiniteType S.p] [QuasiCompact S.p] (hboundary : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary (⨅ i : Fin S.boundary.length, S.boundary.get i)) (hordered : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : S.Z.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ S.boundary.get i)) (hM : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : M.N.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ (S.boundary.get i).comap M.j)) (hP : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : P.N.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ (S.boundary.get i).comap P.j)) (hdim : ∀ (x : M.N) (y : P.N), M.j x = P.j y → ringKrullDim (M.N.presheaf.stalk x) = ringKrullDim (P.N.presheaf.stalk y)) (hequivalent : RestrictedEquivalent M P) : ∀ (T : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (M' P' : Marked T), CommonTestSequence M P M' P' → ∀ (x : M'.N) (y : P'.N), M'.j x = P'.j y → M'.j x ∈ M'.cosupport → P'.j y ∈ P'.cosupport → ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < k → ∀ i : ℕ, (((k + i + 1) * M'.marking : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ (k : ℕ∞) * order M'.ideal x ↔ (((k + i + 1) * P'.marking : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ (k : ℕ∞) * order P'.ideal y
